chunks: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'The sky remains overcast over us in Iraq for a day, two days, and three days. So which day should we fast?' He said: 'Look at the day on which you fasted in the past year, and fast on the fifth day.'

key_terms.تُطْبِقُ: overcast/covers completely — refers to the sky being blocked by clouds, preventing the moon-sighting (ru'yat al-hilal) required to determine the start of Ramadan
key_terms.نَصُومُ: we fast — referring to the obligatory fasting of Ramadan, whose start date depends on confirmed moon-sighting
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْخَامِسِ: the fifth day — the Imam's ruling that one should fast on the fifth day after the reference day from the previous year, as a systematic method to determine Ramadan's start under cloudy conditions

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about determining the start of Ramadan fasting when the sky is cloudy in Iraq?
ai.summary: Imran al-Za'farani asks Imam al-Sadiq (AS) about a practical problem faced in Iraq: when the sky is overcast for multiple consecutive days, making it impossible to sight the new moon (hilal) of Ramadan, which day should believers begin fasting? The Imam provides a pragmatic jurisprudential ruling: refer to the corresponding day from the previous year's calendar and then fast on the fifth day thereafter. This ruling addresses the challenge of moon-sighting in regions with frequent cloud cover, providing a systematic method based on historical precedent rather than waiting indefinitely for clear skies.
